items.zh: 又有邪見，誹謗集諦。謂諸外道作如是計：如彼沙門喬答摩種，為諸弟子所說集諦，此定無有。如是等見，是迷集諦所起邪見。若有見取，取彼諸見以為第一，能得清淨、解脫、出離，是迷集諦所起見取。若於隨順此見諸法所受戒禁，取為第一，能得清淨，廣說如前，是迷集諦戒禁取。餘疑、貪等，如前應知。如是八種煩惱隨眠，迷於集諦，見集所斷。云何迷滅有八隨眠？謂諸沙門、若婆羅門，計邊無邊，不死矯亂諸見一分。
items.en: There is also a wrong view slandering the origination-truth: certain heretics hold that whatever origination-truth the ascetic of the Gautama clan taught his disciples certainly does not exist. Such views are the wrong views arising from delusion about origination. If there is view-attachment grasping these views as foremost, as able to purify, liberate, and release, this is view-attachment arising from delusion about origination. If, in accordance with such a view, one grasps whatever precepts and vows follow from it as foremost, as able to purify, and so on as explained before, this is precept-attachment through delusion about origination. The remaining doubt, greed, and so forth should be understood as before. These eight latent afflictions are delusion about the truth of origination, severed at the path of seeing origination. How does delusion about cessation have eight latent afflictions? Certain ascetics or brahmins compute an edge or no edge, and hold a portion of eel-wriggling views.

items.title: Section: Bliss Mistaken for Nirvana, and the Arhat's Two Virtues Denied

items.zh: 又有沙門、若婆羅門，謂說現法涅槃論者所有邪見。又有邪見，撥無世間真阿羅漢，乃至廣說。彼阿羅漢二德所顯，謂斷及智。此中但取謗斷邪見。又有邪見，誹謗滅諦，謂諸外道，廣說如前。又有橫計諸邪解脫所有邪見。如是諸見，是迷滅諦所起邪見。
items.en: There are also ascetics or brahmins who hold the wrong views of those who teach nirvāṇa attainable in this very life. There is also a wrong view denying that any true arhat exists in the world, and so on at length. That arhat is manifested by two virtues, namely severance and wisdom. Here, only the wrong view denying the virtue of severance is taken. There is also a wrong view slandering the cessation-truth, held by various heretics, explained at length as before. There is also a wrong view falsely computing various mistaken forms of liberation. Such views as these are the wrong views that arise from delusion about cessation.

items.zh: 若有見取，取彼諸見以為第一，廣說如前，是迷滅諦所起見取。若於隨順彼見諸法所受戒禁，取為第一，廣說如前，是迷滅諦戒禁取。所餘貪等，如前應知，唯除瞋恚。

items.title: Section: Fear of Extinction, and Closing All the See-Severed Afflictions

items.zh: 謂於滅諦起怖畏心、起損害心、起恚惱心，如是瞋恚，迷於滅諦。餘如前說。如是八種煩惱隨眠，迷於滅諦，見滅所斷。云何迷道有八隨眠？謂撥無世間真阿羅漢，乃至廣說。此中所有誹謗一切智為導首有為無漏，當知此見，是迷道諦所起邪見。又諸沙門、若婆羅門，不死矯亂邪見一分，亦迷於道。又諸外道謗道邪見，彼謂沙門喬答摩種，為諸弟子說出離道，實非出離，由此不能盡出離苦。佛所施設無我之見，及所受持戒禁隨法，是惡邪道，非正妙道。如是亦名迷道邪見。又彼外道作如是計：我等所行若行、若道，是真行道，能盡、能出一切諸苦。如是亦名迷道邪見。若有見取，取彼邪見以為第一，能得清淨、解脫、出離，如是名為迷道見取。若於隨順彼見諸法所受戒禁，取為第一，能得清淨、解脫、出離，是名迷道戒禁取。所餘貪等迷道煩惱，如迷滅諦道理應知。如是八種煩惱隨眠，迷於道諦，見道所斷。
items.en: Generating a mind of dread, a mind of harm, and a mind of resentful anguish towards the cessation-truth — such hatred is delusion about cessation. How does delusion about the path have eight latent afflictions? Denying that any true arhat exists in the world, and so on at length. Here, slandering everything conditioned and undefiled that has wisdom as its leader — this view should be known as the wrong view arising from delusion about the path. Certain ascetics or brahmins also hold a portion of eel-wriggling wrong view, which likewise is delusion about the path. Certain heretics further slander the path, holding that whatever path of renunciation the ascetic of the Gautama clan taught his disciples is not truly renunciation at all, and cannot fully lead beings out of suffering; that the view of selflessness the Buddha established, together with its accompanying precepts, is a wicked, deviant path rather than the true and wondrous one. This too is called delusion about the path. Those same heretics also compute that whatever practice or path they themselves follow is the true path, able to exhaust and escape all suffering. This too is called delusion about the path. Thus the outflows severed at the path of seeing have now all been explained.

items.title: Section: Why Some Afflictions Take a Lifetime — The Deeper-Rooted Four

items.zh: 如是已說見斷諸漏。云何修道所斷諸漏？謂欲界瞋恚，三界三種貪、慢、無明，由彼長時修習正道，方能得斷，是故名為修道所斷。又彼煩惱界界地地皆有三品，謂下中上。能斷之道亦有三品。下品之道能斷上品修斷諸漏，中能斷中，上道斷下。
items.en: The outflows severed at the path of seeing have thus been explained. What are the outflows severed by the path of cultivation? Hatred in the desire realm, and the three kinds of greed, conceit, and ignorance across the three realms — since these are severed only through long cultivation of the correct path, they are called severed by cultivation. Moreover, these afflictions, in every realm and every stage, each have three grades: lower, middle, and upper. The antidote path capable of severing them likewise has three grades. The lower grade of the path severs the upper grade of outflow severed by cultivation; the middle severs the middle; the upper path severs the lower.

items.title: Section: Closing Confusion-Severance, and the Five Objects Affliction Actually References

items.zh: 又彼修道所斷諸漏，於有漏事任運而轉，長時堅固，於自所迷事難可解脫。是名建立煩惱雜染迷斷差別。復次，即如所說見、修所斷諸漏煩惱，當知略有五種所緣。一、緣邪分別所起事境，二、緣見境，三、緣戒禁境，四、緣自分別所起名境，五、緣任運堅固事境。此中，若緣苦、集事境所有諸漏，是緣邪分別所起事境。見取、貪等見斷諸漏，除疑，是緣見境。戒禁取，是緣戒禁境。緣滅、道境及緣不同分界境所有諸漏，是緣自分別所起名境。何以故？非此煩惱能緣滅、道，亦不能緣不同分界，非無所緣故。修所斷漏，是緣自任運堅固事境。
items.en: Those outflows severed by the path of cultivation operate spontaneously with respect to what arises through affliction, remain fixed for a long time, and are difficult to be freed from with respect to the very matters they are confused about. This is called establishing the confusion-and-severance distinction of affliction defilement. Moreover, as already explained, the outflows and afflictions severed by seeing and by cultivation should be known, in brief, to have five kinds of object. First, an object arisen through wrong discrimination. Second, a view-object. Third, a precept-object. Fourth, a name-object arisen through one's own discrimination. Fifth, a spontaneous, persistent object. Among these, the outflows referencing the objects of suffering and origination reference an object arisen through wrong discrimination. View-attachment, greed, and the rest of the outflows severed by seeing, apart from doubt, reference a view-object. Precept-attachment references a precept-object. Outflows referencing the objects of cessation and the path, and those referencing a dissimilar realm, reference a name-object arisen through one's own discrimination. Outflows severed by cultivation reference one's own spontaneous, persistent object.

blocks.text: Afflictions confused about cessation and the path, and the four deep-rooted afflictions that take long cultivation to cut.
The views that arise from not seeing how suffering comes about.

Master Cháng Bǎi: this view holds that one attains nirvāṇa with the present aggregates; it comes from ignorance of the truth of cessation. Others slander the arhat's complete severing of affliction. (Untranslated, 0624b07: view-attachment and precept-attachment that arise from delusion about cessation.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: thinking that in nirvāṇa the self and body are gone, one feels terror and anger. The severing wisdom is conditioned and uncontaminated; cessation is unconditioned.

Master Cháng Bǎi: these four afflictions must be cut by long cultivation; afflictions make merit "leak away", and so are called outflows. The weaker path cuts the coarser affliction; the strongest path, the subtlest.
Master Cháng Bǎi: these afflictions run spontaneously with the aggregates, innate and firm. Doubt ranges over objects raised by one's own mind through names.
"Fear of nirvāṇa" is honest: if we cling to being someone, the end of clinging looks like death. The treatise names this fear as an affliction, to be seen through.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the theory of nirvāṇa here and now, and why is it delusion about cessation?
options: it means the arhat's present bliss, a correct teaching
it holds nirvāṇa comes only after death
it holds there are no afflictions
it holds nirvāṇa attainable with the present aggregates, arising from ignorance of cessation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this holds that one obtains nirvāṇa with the present aggregates, without waiting for death, and arises from ignorance of the truth of cessation. The English "nirvāṇa attainable in this very life" should not be confused with the arhat's actual nirvāṇa with remainder.

quiz.q: What are the arhat's two virtues, and which denial counts under cessation?
options: concentration and wisdom; only denial of wisdom, cessation being wisdom's culmination, and denial of severance belonging under the path
severance and wisdom; here only denial of severance is taken
ethics and concentration; only denial of ethics
compassion and wisdom; only denial of compassion
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: wrong ideas about the arhat's complete severing of affliction and accomplishing of nirvāṇa are the slander of severance; only with the seeds of the three poisons permanently severed is one an arhat. Denial of the arhat's wisdom falls under the path at §38.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain dread and hostility towards cessation?
options: it is a practitioner's reverent awe
fear of falling into hell
fear of losing wealth
thinking nirvāṇa means no self or body left, one feels terror and displeasure
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one thinks that in nirvāṇa the self and the body are gone, feels terror, and gives rise to harm and anger, unhappy at the idea of nirvāṇa. This relates to the fear of cessation that keeps beings attached to existence.

quiz.q: The English has "slandering the unconditioned, undefiled wisdom." What is wrong?
options: 有為 is rendered "unconditioned," the reverse; the lecture says severing wisdom is conditioned and uncontaminated
nothing: everything uncontaminated is unconditioned, 有為 being a scribal error rightly fixed, the lecture also calling the path unconditioned
"undefiled" should be "clean"
"slandering" should be "praising"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the severing wisdom is conditioned and uncontaminated, and it brings beings to arhatship. Cessation is the unconditioned; the path is conditioned though uncontaminated. "Unconditioned" is therefore the reverse, and would make this denial fall under cessation. "As productive of nothing" is also an addition.

quiz.q: What are the outflows severed by cultivation, and why so named?
options: desire-realm hatred and greed, conceit, and ignorance of the three realms, severed only through long cultivation
the five views and doubt, the deepest ideas needing long practice
shamelessness and heedlessness
all ten root afflictions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these four afflictions are deep-rooted and must be severed by long cultivation of the correct path; afflictions make beings leak away merit, and so are called outflows. Views and doubt go at the path of seeing, while these innate four remain.

quiz.q: How do the three grades of path and of affliction correspond?
options: upper severs upper, middle middle, lower lower, strength having to match, so that weak paths cannot sever strong afflictions, unrelated to coarseness
any grade severs all at once
the lower path severs upper-grade outflows, middle severs middle, the upper path severs lower-grade
only the upper grade severs
quiz.why: The treatise pairs them crosswise. Master Cháng Bǎi repeats this: the lower-grade path severs the upper grade, and the upper-grade path the lower. Coarse afflictions go first, and the most subtle last, as with washing a cloth. The English is correct.

quiz.q: The English has "being confused about their own ever-present object." What is the problem?
options: no problem: the object always exists, so "ever-present" is a needed gloss, the point being confusion
"ever-present" is added and the structure inverted: the Chinese says it is hard to be freed from the confused object
"confused" should be "angry"
"object" should be "goal"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these afflictions run spontaneously with the aggregates, innate, firm over a long time, continuing from birth to death. The confused object is the aggregates, and the claim is that it is hard to get free of them. The English adds "ever-present" and subordinates the point.

quiz.q: Under which object fall outflows taking cessation and the path, and what about doubt?
options: a persistent object; doubt falls under precept-objects, cessation and the path being fixed and doubt concerning precepts
a name-object from one's own discrimination; doubt is excepted from view-objects, ranging over both
a view-object; doubt under wrong-discrimination objects
a precept-object; doubt under name-objects
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these are objects raised by one's own mind through names and discrimination; doubt, undecided this way or that, ranges over view-objects and objects from wrong discrimination. This also fits §13, where a lower realm takes higher realms only through names.
